summary: This article explains how llamas and alpacas are related to camels, how they are suited to life high in the Andes, and how people have used them for thousands of years.
introduce: Read the title “Camels' Cousins: Llamas and Alpacas” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: an animal or person from long ago that later ones came from
tamed and raised by people instead of living wild
a thin thread of hair or plant material that can be spun into cloth

challengeTerms.def: a member of the animal family that includes camels, llamas, alpacas, guanacos, and vicuñas
the process of taming wild plants or animals so people can raise them
to cover or protect something so that heat does not escape

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that llamas and alpacas are more useful to people than camels are? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how llamas and alpacas are suited to life high in the Andes.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review ancestor, domesticated, and fiber, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use camelid, domestication, and insulate in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
